options.note: Medium-up swing in F, built like a jazz standard: 32 bars, A A B A. Turnarounds with sixth chords, a diminished passing chord, a bluesy IV to iv turn. The bridge goes round the cycle of fifths (A7 D7 G7 C7) with the same little phrase moved onto each chord, and every phrase slides down by half steps into the next. Muted trumpet, then clarinet; walking bass, ride cymbal, piano comping.

options.title: Now

topics.title: Ways of doing the riso print (made by Fable)

rounds.question: Six takes on the game's own riso print (same cream paper, inks, dots and misprint), several with dots between now and the big-dot look. Which one, or keep Now? Notes on mixing them welcome (D's riso quirks can go on top of another).
rounds.found: Made by a Fable helper. Dot sizes (times a game pixel): Now 1.3, A 1.4, B 1.7, C 1.65, D 1.7, E 1.7, F 1.85 (the comic big-dot was 2.3). It found much of the busyness in Now is per-pixel speckle and paper flecks (the night sky looks like extra stars), and every option drops that. The differences are small: the side-by-side sheet (first picture on Now) is the best way to compare, and dots read differently on the Pocket 6. Overtime reprints work in all six. Its favourite: F (solid darks), then B for the plainest in-between.

rounds.question: Five ways to animate your logo as the studio intro, each about 5 seconds long. In every one the pink wave moves thin, rubbery and a bit odd, like audio, before it settles into your logo. Which one, or which parts should be mixed? The sounds are first drafts and are easy to change.

options.title: Plucked string
options.note: The wave starts as a thin, still string. It gets plucked and rings in its harmonics, wobbling through odd shapes. Then it settles into the logo shape and swells up to full thickness. The name fades in. Sound: a plucked bass string, then a soft chord and a bell.

options.title: Oscilloscope
options.note: A thin, glowing line jitters like a voice on a scope, then tunes in and locks onto the logo shape with a glow. The name types in letter by letter. Sound: a wobbly voice-like bleep that tunes to one clean note, with clicks as the letters type.

options.title: Rubber band
options.note: A pink blob stretches out into a thin, wriggly band, pulled tight. It snaps into the wave and jiggles like rubber before it settles. The name drops in. Sound: a stretchy boing, a snap and a wobble, then a soft thud.

options.title: Idle loop
options.note: The wave rolls along like a loop playing, thinning and thickening as it breathes. It slows to a stop on the logo shape. "studios" spreads out under the name. Sound: a little looping arpeggio that lands on a held chord.

options.title: Wobbly pen
options.note: A thin, shaky pen line draws the wave from left to right. Then it puffs up like jelly to full thickness and wobbles. The name fades in. Sound: a pen scratch, a rising whoop and a jelly wobble, then a chime.

rounds.found: Picked D. Note (sent in chat): too long; drop the part where it moves left; a smooth entrance into the quick rightward part through to the end; did not like how the text came in. (The note was lost by a bug in this page, now fixed.)

options.title: Tape loop

options.title: Rubber synth

options.title: Beat drop

rounds.found: Upright, the game takes about a third of an iPhone 15's screen (32-33%; the most a full-width 4:3 game can take is 34.6%). Sideways it takes about 58%. Fable checked every button and the screen on the iPhone SE, 15 and 15 Pro Max, upright and sideways, with and without the notch and home bar: nothing overlaps, nothing runs off the screen, and every button is at least 44px. Its favourites: H2 (grey brick) of the handhelds, and R2 (heavy ink) of the riso, with R1 the safe pick if R2 is too busy. The iPhone SE picture is the third on each. Picked: H1, cream classic. In the game from build 180.

rounds.question: Fable looked at why the stages feel unplanned. All five are the same picture: four full catwalks, twelve containers in the same grid, and ladders that drift a column from stage to stage, so they look almost symmetrical, which reads as a mistake. Its fix: every stage an exact mirror or an exact upside-down copy, ladders only on a few set columns, and gaps that mean something. Here is 1-1 Harbor Pier (in its day). Play each with "Play in game": START GAME goes straight to this stage. Which one, or which parts to mix?
rounds.found: Every version passes all the fast tests, and a bot clears each one. The death counts are bots (8 beginners and 8 good players per stage), a small sample, so only a rough guide to difficulty. Nobody has played these by hand yet. If a new layout goes in, the title demos get new seeds. Picked: A. In the game from build 187.

rounds.question: Fable looked at why the stages feel unplanned. All five are the same picture: four full catwalks, twelve containers in the same grid, and ladders that drift a column from stage to stage, so they look almost symmetrical, which reads as a mistake. Its fix: every stage an exact mirror or an exact upside-down copy, ladders only on a few set columns, and gaps that mean something. Here is 1-3 Conveyor Line (in its day). Play each with "Play in game": START GAME goes straight to this stage. Which one, or which parts to mix?
rounds.found: Every version passes all the fast tests, and a bot clears each one. The death counts are bots (8 beginners and 8 good players per stage), a small sample, so only a rough guide to difficulty. Nobody has played these by hand yet. If a new layout goes in, the title demos get new seeds. Picked: A. In the game from build 187.

rounds.question: Same song, same notes, same band: only the keyboard that plays the tune and the left hand changes. Which sound? (You can pick one, or mix: say which in the note, e.g. one sound for the tune and another for the left hand.)
rounds.found: The first 48 seconds of the song each (the intro and the first strain twice), recorded from the game's own synth, loudness-matched so none sounds better just by being louder. Picked: the marimba (G) while you play, the honky-tonk piano as it is on the menus and the pause menu. In the game from build 199.

options.title: As it is: honky-tonk
options.note: The ragtime piano in the game now: a bright, buzzy synth piano playing both hands.

options.title: Upright piano
options.note: Rounder and warmer: a soft hammer, notes ring a little longer and darken as they fade. The most like a real parlor piano.

options.title: Tack piano (saloon)
options.note: The old saloon sound: three strings tuned a little apart for the honky-tonk wobble, bright, with a tack on each hammer.

options.title: Electric piano
options.note: A Rhodes-style tine: soft and round, a little bell on each note that melts away, and a slow shimmer. Smooth and cool, more lounge than saloon.

options.title: Clavinet
options.note: A funky plucked string: bright and snappy, each note closing fast. Gives the rag a bouncier, 70s feel.

options.title: Chiptune
options.note: Old game console: the tune on a square-ish pulse, the left hand on the triangle bass. Very retro arcade.

options.title: Marimba
options.note: Warm wooden bars: a soft knock and a quick ring, the left hand deep and round. Light and playful.

rounds.question: The last three seconds of POWER RUSH counted down in big numbers, so you know it's ending. Which look?
rounds.found: Each clip is the end of a rush on 1-2 (with sound: every option has the same beep on each number and a lower double beep when the rush ends, so only the look differs; tell me if you want the sound changed too). The play copies start on 1-2 and give you a POWER RUSH at the start of every stage. Picked: C, the badge, with a rising whoosh under it that cuts off the moment the rush ends. In the game from build 202.

topics.title: Rider ready: showing who would ride a container down

rounds.question: When an enemy is standing where he'd ride a container down if it dropped now, the container shows it. Which look?
rounds.found: It uses exactly the game's rider rule, so it only lights up when dropping the container now really would take them with it (it also lights for an enemy climbing a ladder just above it, since he'd ride too). Each clip has the same scene on 1-1, with the game's sounds: two Pratts walk onto a container, Buck horns them, then walks it and sends both down as riders. The play copies are the normal game with that option on. Picked: B, the rider pips. In the game from build 209.

options.title: Rim glow
options.note: The container's outline glows pink and pulses while anyone's on it. More riders make a thicker rim.

images.label: Two Pratts ride a container down

options.title: Rider pips
options.note: A small pink tag on the container's top corner with one dot per enemy who'd ride (up to four).

images.label: Two Pratts ride a container down

options.title: Down arrows
options.note: Pink chevrons run downward under the container, below the catwalk, saying it'll take them down.

images.label: Two Pratts ride a container down

options.title: What it's worth
options.note: The rider bonus it would pay floats above everyone's heads: RIDER +300 for one, +1,500 for two (before the combo).

images.label: Two Pratts ride a container down

options.title: Pink lamps
options.note: The work lamps on top of the container glow and flash pink while anyone's on it.

images.label: Two Pratts ride a container down

rounds.question: The rider pips move down onto the catwalk under the container so they don't cover the play area, and the other end shows, in blue, who it would squash if it dropped now. Which way?
rounds.found: Riders count exactly as the game does. Squashes count anyone in its path from here down to where it would stop (one catwalk, plus one more per rider). That one is a forecast: an enemy can still walk out from under it while it falls. In the clip the yellow container has two stunned Pratts on it (pink, 2) and one under it (blue, 1); the pink one above shows blue 2 because it would squash the two stunned ones. Same scene and sounds in each clip; the play copies are the game with that option on. Picked: A, tags on the catwalk; past four it's four dots and a plus at the growing end (left for pink, right for blue). In the game from build 210.

options.title: Tags on the catwalk
options.note: The same little tags, lying on the yellow catwalk under the container's ends: pink on the right for riders, blue on the left for squashes, one cream dot per enemy.

options.title: Lit rivets
options.note: No tag: the catwalk's own rivets under the container light up, one per enemy, glowing pink from the right end (riders) and blue from the left end (squashes).

options.title: Tags under the catwalk
options.note: The tags hang just below the yellow beam under the container's ends, like labels clipped to it: pink right for riders, blue left for squashes.

topics.title: New best and on the board, without the stamp

rounds.question: How should the game-over card say you got a new best score, or made the board?
rounds.found: Each clip shows the card twice, with sound: first a new best (1,234,560), then the same score making the board in third place. Every option comes in with a ding once the score has finished counting up, and none of them sits over the score. Picked: C, the ribbon turns over. In the game from build 216.

options.title: Now: the stamp
options.note: The tilted rubber stamp at the card's top right, as it is (it runs into the score in the millions).

images.label: New best, then on the board

options.title: A tag on the rule
options.note: A yellow tag pops onto the dotted line under the score: NEW BEST! or ON THE BOARD!, with a shine running across it now and then.

images.label: New best, then on the board

options.title: The label changes
options.note: Once the score has counted up, FINAL SCORE above it flips to NEW BEST! (or ON THE BOARD!) in pink, with little sparkles either side.

images.label: New best, then on the board

options.title: The ribbon turns over
options.note: The pink GAME OVER ribbon flips like a sign to a yellow NEW BEST! (or ON THE BOARD!) ribbon.

rounds.question: When an enemy is stunned, how should his stars (and the gull's feathers) move?
rounds.found: A to E move the real stars lifted out of each dizzy picture (Pratt, the Watchman and the Forklift have them; the Captain has none; the gull has feathers). F draws new stars like the title's Captain. Left to right in each clip: Pratt, the Watchman, the Captain, the Forklift, the gull, all stunned on 3-1. No sound in these clips. Picked: E. In the game from build 219.

options.title: Now
options.note: The stars sit still in each dizzy picture (the gull's feathers too); only the figure wobbles.

options.title: They circle
options.note: The picture's own stars ride round a ring over his head, passing behind it at the back. The gull's feathers circle him the same way.

options.title: They twinkle
options.note: The picture's own stars stay put but each bobs, swells and tilts in turn. The gull's feathers sway.

options.title: They spin
options.note: The picture's own stars spin on the spot, each at its own pace, with a little bob. The gull's feathers tumble.

options.title: They hop in turn
options.note: The picture's own stars hop up and pop one after another, left to right, round and round. The feathers too.

options.title: Circle, stars for all
options.note: Like A, and the Captain (who has no stars in his picture) gets three drawn stars circling his cap.

options.title: Drawn stars, like the title
options.note: The pictures' stars go; every stunned enemy gets the three drawn stars circling his head that the Captain has after he bonks into the container in the title. The gull's feathers circle.
